QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_35

question.text: Under SAS-400, the 'LGBTQIA+ inclusion' indicator in workplace programmes requires reporting:

answer.text: The sexual orientation of every employee
Aggregate, anonymised self-identification of LGBTQIA+ employees with explicit opt-in consent, plus policy-level indicators (anti-discrimination policy, benefits parity, ERG support)

explanation.text: The Logic: Conceptually, measuring LGBTQIA+ workplace inclusion in a privacy-respecting way relies on aggregate, anonymised self-identification of LGBTQIA+ employees with explicit opt-in consent, combined with policy-level indicators such as anti-discrimination policies, benefits parity, and Employee Resource Group (ERG) support. This pairs an outcome-style metric with an enabling-environment view. The Trap: Reporting the sexual orientation of every employee violates privacy and consent norms. The CEO's personal views are not evidence and cannot be assured. Reporting only policy text omits the workforce-level metric. Note: The Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) identifies SAS-400 as the gender-equality / women / LGBTQIA+ thematic area but does not detail an "opt-in anonymised LGBTQIA+ self-identification + anti-discrimination policy + benefits parity + ERG + minimum-cell reporting" framework on the pages reviewed. The framing above reflects general inclusion-reporting practice (e.g., DPDP Act-aligned privacy and BRSR-style diversity disclosures).
